drhp.business: Indian Emulsifiers Limited manufactures esters, amphoterics, phosphate esters, imidazolines, wax emulsions, SMO and PIBSA emulsifiers and related intermediates, operating from its manufacturing facility at MIDC Lote Parshuram, Ratnagiri, Maharashtra. The Company focuses on customised formulations and contract manufacturing in close partnership with institutional clients, serving the food, cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, home care, industrial cleaning, textiles, mining, oilfield, agriculture and paints sectors.
drhp.end_markets: Food|Cosmetics|Pharmaceuticals|Home Care|Industrial Cleaning|Textiles|Mining|Oilfield|Agriculture|Paints|Australia (mining emulsifiers)|United States (Oil & Gas, Food, Technical Textile Auxiliaries, Water Treatment)
drhp.expansion: IEML has expanded installed capacity five-fold at its MIDC Lote Parshuram facility, from 2,400 MTPA to 12,000 MTPA, through phased addition of reactors and process infrastructure (2,400 MTPA to 4,800 MTPA in FY24, 7,800 MTPA in FY25, and 12,000 MTPA in FY26). The Company is developing a Greenfield facility at Plot C-3, Lote Parshuram MIDC, on an adjoining plot acquired in February 2026, expected to be substantially operational by the end of FY27, adding a theoretical capacity of approximately 400-500 metric tonnes per month with further expansion headroom of 300-500 tonnes identified on the same site. A separate adjoining plot, also acquired in February 2026, is being developed for tripled QC/R&D space and certified food-grade production infrastructure, expected to add approximately 200-250 tonnes per month of sellable capacity once operational and certified, likely in late FY27 or early FY28. Internationally, the Company established a wholly owned Australian subsidiary (Southern Emulsifiers Solutions Pty Ltd, targeting mining-emulsifier demand) and a wholly owned US subsidiary (Polaris Specialty Chemicals Inc., targeting Oil & Gas, Food, Technical Textile Auxiliaries and Water Treatment markets) during FY26.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Deliberate volume-led growth, geographic expansion and customer-base broadening drove FY26 performance, with EBITDA margin moderating as a result of these choices.
- Management expects gradual, quarter-on-quarter improvement in EBITDA margin as procurement scale benefits and stronger supplier terms materialise, assuming stable macroeconomic and raw material price conditions; no specific FY27 margin target has been given pending finalisation of the proposed rights issue and capital allocation.
- Customer mix shifted toward larger accounts with longer standard credit cycles, raising debtor days; management states improved creditor terms from strengthened procurement leverage kept the overall cash conversion cycle broadly stable despite this shift.
- A strategic inventory build-up was made toward the end of FY26 in response to Middle East supply disruption and raw material price volatility; management states supply conditions have improved since April 2026 with cost increases passed through to customers.
- Company's access to conventional debt financing is constrained by its scale and collateral position as an SME issuer, per management commentary on fundraising rationale.

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: IEML has expanded installed capacity five-fold at its MIDC Lote Parshuram facility, from 2,400 MTPA to 12,000 MTPA, through phased addition of reactors and process infrastructure (2,400 MTPA to 4,800 MTPA in FY24, 7,800 MTPA in FY25, and 12,000 MTPA in FY26). The Company is developing a Greenfield facility at Plot C-3, Lote Parshuram MIDC, on an adjoining plot acquired in February 2026, expected to be substantially operational by the end of FY27, adding a theoretical capacity of approximately 400-500 metric tonnes per month with further expansion headroom of 300-500 tonnes identified on the same site. A separate adjoining plot, also acquired in February 2026, is being developed for tripled QC/R&D space and certified food-grade production infrastructure, expected to add approximately 200-250 tonnes per month of sellable capacity once operational and certified, likely in late FY27 or early FY28. Internationally, the Company established a wholly owned Australian subsidiary (Southern Emulsifiers Solutions Pty Ltd, targeting mining-emulsifier demand) and a wholly owned US subsidiary (Polaris Specialty Chemicals Inc., targeting Oil & Gas, Food, Technical Textile Auxiliaries and Water Treatment markets) during FY26.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- distribution: Diversified international footprint reduces dependence on any single market — evidence: wholly owned Australian subsidiary (Southern Emulsifiers Solutions Pty Ltd) and US subsidiary (Polaris Specialty Chemicals Inc.), with operations spanning 9 countries.
- customer lock-in: Application knowledge and customisation capability creates deeper customer relationships and higher entry barriers — evidence: Australian technical staff with over 40 years of mining-specific expertise supporting customised solutions in mining-related segments.
- technology: Manufacturing flexibility allows capacity scaling without significant new capex — evidence: single facility with multiple flexible reactors operating across 10-250°C and 5-8 kg/cm², enabling capacity to scale from 2,400 MTPA to 12,000 MTPA primarily through incremental additions.
- licence/regulatory: Quality certifications support entry into regulated and international markets — evidence: ISO 9001:2015, Kosher and Halal certifications supported by in-house QC and application laboratories — against it: the Company remains partly restricted from selling food-grade-capable products into the food industry today due to current facility certification constraints.
- scale: Broad, diversified product portfolio reduces dependence on any single product or end-use segment — evidence: over 125 chemicals across 7+ chemistry families and 8+ industry verticals, of which approximately 60-70 products are actively sold.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Company faces price volatility dependent on crude oil prices; the SWOT notes this is expected to be partly minimized as both input and output prices are impacted, but it remains a disclosed structural exposure.
- As exports grow, sudden Rupee depreciation or appreciation is disclosed as having a short-term impact on realization.
- Company discloses a threat from competition using new technologies from large global multinationals.
- Regulatory challenges, government policies and tax procedures are disclosed as capable of impacting margins.
- The Australian subsidiary experienced a temporary slowdown from Australian floods (January 2026) and a fuel shortage (March 2026) affecting customer offtake, and the US subsidiary (Polaris) currently lacks local banking facilities, requiring working capital support via extended shipment credit from the parent until a Board-approved capital infusion is completed.
- Debtor days rose from approximately 110 to 131 as the Company's customer mix shifted toward larger accounts with longer standard credit cycles, disclosed as part of MD&A financial performance commentary.
- The proposed rights issue and related investment in Chemical Brothers Enterprises Private Limited (a related party via the Managing Director's stake) drew shareholder concerns on pricing, timing and rationale, alongside promoter shareholding dilution from approximately 48% to approximately 32.64% following the first rights issue.
- The Company remains partly restricted from selling its food-grade-capable products into the food industry today due to current facility certification constraints, pending completion of new certified food-grade production infrastructure.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Commission the Greenfield C3 facility, expanding manufacturing and product capabilities.
- Scale the Australian subsidiary (Southern Emulsifiers Solutions Pty Ltd) toward its three-year cumulative revenue target, with two additional targeted customers expected to come online in FY27.
- Build out the US subsidiary (Polaris Specialty Chemicals Inc.), including a Board-approved working capital infusion, to reduce reliance on extended shipment credit from the parent as it scales.
- Complete certification and commissioning of new food-grade production infrastructure to enter the food industry, from which the Company is currently partly restricted.
- Continue to improve operational efficiency across the working capital cycle.
